title: Misery
tagline: Paul Sheldon used to write for a living. Now he's writing to stay alive.
about: A famous novelist crashes in a Colorado blizzard and wakes up in the farmhouse of his number one fan, who will not let him leave.
cue: Pour the champagne when Paul finishes the book and sends Annie for a glass.

Velvety tomato soup and cheddar toasts.How to make it30g butter1 brown onion, diced2 garlic cloves, sliced800g tinned whole tomatoes500ml vegetable stock1 tsp caster sugar125ml pouring cream8 slices of baguette100g vintage cheddar, gratedSoften the onion and garlic in the butter.Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes.Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season.Pile the cheddar on the baguette slices and grill until bubbling, then float them on the soup.Dirty birdie barbecue wingsAnnie calls Paul a dirty bird. Sticky smoky wings and ranch dip.How to make it1kg chicken wings, jointed1 tbsp baking powder2 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp garlic powder125ml smoky barbecue sauce1 tbsp honey125g sour cream2 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 tbsp chives, snipped1 garlic clove, crushedPat the wings dry and toss with the baking powder, paprika, garlic powder and salt.Bake on a rack at 220°C, turning once, until crisp.Toss with the warmed barbecue sauce and honey.Mix the sour cream, mayo, chives and garlic into a ranch dip and serve.Buttered corn on the cobAnnie never swears at the feed store.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsSnowed-in meatloaf with buttery mashPaul's pills go into Annie's wine. Glazed beef meatloaf and green beans.How to make it800g beef mince1 brown onion, grated2 garlic cloves, crushed1 egg60g fresh breadcrumbs60ml milk, plus 125ml for the mash2 tsp thyme leaves125ml tomato sauce2 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp apple cider vinegar1kg floury potatoes, peeled50g butter200g green beansSoak the breadcrumbs in 60ml milk, then mix with the beef, onion, garlic, egg, thyme and salt and shape into a loaf in a lined tin.Stir the tomato sauce, sugar and vinegar and spread half over the loaf.Bake at 180°C, glazing again halfway, until cooked through.Meanwhile boil and mash the potatoes with the butter and milk and steam the beans.Rest the loaf for 10 minutes, slice thickly and serve with the mash and beans.Silver Creek beef pot roastAnnie's pet sow is called Misery. Fork-tender beef pot roast.How to make it1.5kg beef chuck roast2 tbsp vegetable oil2 brown onions, cut in wedges4 carrots, in chunks600g small potatoes3 garlic cloves2 tbsp tomato paste2 tbsp plain flour750ml beef stock3 thyme sprigs2 bay leavesSeason the beef and brown it well all over in the oil, then lift out.Soften the onions and garlic, stir in the tomato paste and flour, then the stock.Return the beef with the thyme and bay, cover and cook at 160°C for 2 and a half hours.Add the carrots and potatoes and cook until everything is tender.Slice or pull the beef and serve with the vegetables and gravy.Something SweetDue south self-saucing chocolate puddingThe penguin always faces due south. Chocolate sponge over its own fudge sauce.How to make it150g self-raising flour150g caster sugar30g cocoa powder, plus 2 tbsp for the topping185ml milk80g butter, melted1 egg1 tsp vanilla extract150g brown sugar375ml boiling water300ml vanilla ice creamWhisk the flour, caster sugar and 30g cocoa, then whisk in the milk, butter, egg and vanilla and spread in a buttered dish.Mix the brown sugar with the rest of the cocoa and scatter it over the batter.Pour the boiling water gently over the back of a spoon.Bake at 180°C until the top is firm and the sauce bubbles underneath.Rest 5 minutes and serve with ice cream.To DrinkFinished manuscript champagnePaul's ritual when a book is done.
